text: for the management of postop- erative shivering including the central and respiratory stimulant doxapram, the α2-agonist clonidine, and the opioid analgesic pethidine.2,4,5 Reviews have discussed1-4 a number of other opi- oids that have been tried including morphine, alfentanil, butorph- anol, fentanyl, and sufentanil but studies suggest that not all opi- oids are effective or that some may only be effective when given epidurally. However, this may be due to the use of insufficient doses rather than a true difference between opioids.6 Tramadol and nefopam have also been tried.2,5 Neuromuscular blockers have been used after cardiac surgery in order to reduce cardio- vascular stress.7 Vecuronium might be preferable to pancuro- nium as it does not increase myocardial work and may be asso- ciated with fewer complications.8 However, as profound neuromuscular block is required to inhibit shivering, repeated or higher doses of vecuronium might be required to prevent recur- rence. Other drugs that have been investigated include ketanser- in,2 ketamine,9 and magnesium sulfate.2 1. Crossley AWA. Postoperative shivering. Br J Hosp Med 1993; 49: 204–8. 2. Alfonsi P.
